I met lovely clients, Counsellors and trainers and staff. I really really wish I had discovered the Tree House first and not wasted the last 15 years of my life ! I stayed for 6 weeks at The Treehouse Retreat — and yes, it was truly life-changing for me.

Coming from a phase where professional and personal responsibilities had completely defined my identity, I was battling anxiety, chronic depression and an overall low phase in life. This retreat gave me the calmness and space I desperately needed, while also helping me build a routine — with daily workouts and simple brain exercises.

More than that, I learned to practice the basics: empathy, kindness, and love — which made me more mindful and humble each day. The weekly Thursday excursions felt like moments of freedom within the structure, thoughtfully designed within time slots.

I highly recommend this place to anyone prepared to put in the work to become a better version of themselves. But let me clarify — this is not a place of instant magic. The team equips you with the right tools, but it is entirely up to you to practice, apply, and build positivity from them.

The food, while simple and sometimes monotonous, is part of the process — and as the team rightly says, “trust the process.” I personally committed to a digital detox during my time here and brought along a few long-awaited books — which turned out to be the perfect companion for my downtime.

One of my most significant realizations during this journey was: acceptance of your weaknesses can make life much easier. It’s essential to accelerate your strengths, but equally important to develop coping mechanisms for your weaknesses.

Brain mapping was another eye-opener for me. I completed 20 sessions of neurofeedback in 6 weeks. However, the experts did mention that meaningful results usually show after 60 sessions — so I would suggest opting for these only if truly necessary and committed for 60 sessions.

The staff here is incredibly friendly and supportive. I’m especially grateful for the sessions I had with Tony and John — both of whom guided me through invaluable reflections and personal revelations.

Overall, my experience was transformative — but like everything in life, you’ll only get as much as you’re willing to put in.

When I first got here I thought I just needed like, a break from weed you know? Figured it was about cutting back or whatever, maybe learning some tricks to deal with stuff. But what actually went down was way deeper than I expected.

I've been dealing with depression and anxiety pretty much my whole life. Weed became my go-to for numbing all that out, but it never actually fixed anything - just made things... quieter I guess. At The Treehouse they really pushed me to dig into the stuff underneath. All the old wounds and self-doubt and fear. God it was painful. There were definitely times I wanted to just bail, but I started realizing the real fight wasn't even with cannabis. It was with all these parts of myself I'd been running from for years.
Writing my story down... man that nearly destroyed me. Had to look at all these moments I've been trying so hard to forget, left me feeling completely raw and exposed. But slowly - and I mean slowly - I began seeing these patterns. How the depression would just drag me down into this hole, how anxiety kept me totally paralyzed, and how weed was basically just this band-aid I slapped on everything.

The Treehouse didn't like, magically cure me or anything. That's not how recovery works I guess. But it gave me tools and honesty and just... space to finally stop running from myself. I'm leaving here knowing the real work happens at home, and honestly? For the first time in forever I actually think I can handle it.

Treehouse's multi-faceted approach has helped me in ways I cannot describe. The many different therapies included in the program allows me to gain insights and experience a wide variety of tools with which I can effectively deal with overwhelming emotions and situations. Everything ties together to create a strong, well-equipped support system.

The weekly excursions are very well-planned and thought out. Very much a welcome break in the weekly routine, though the schedule is excellent.

The staff are excellent. Everyone is very helpful, friendly, and professional. The location also is quite serene and lush. My stay here has been one of calm and warmth—vital for my journey in unearthing and healing past trauma.

My experience at here was truly life-changing.The holistic program, combining evidence-based therapies with yoga and mindfulness practices, was tailored to individual needs and guided by knowledgeable staff who offered personalized care and encouragement. The community atmosphere was uplifting, fostering deep connections with fellow residents.

Leaving Treehouse Thailand, I feel equipped with the tools and mindset for continued sobriety and am immensely grateful for the transformative journey and supportive community I found there.

Spent 6 weeks at Treehouse and it was lifechanging. I arrived burnt-out, fearful and anxious and left super fit, healthy and empowered. The location is amazing, on the River Ping with stunning gardens, mountain views and an icy refreshing pool. The rooms are amazing traditional teak huts with incredibly comfy fluffy four poster beds. The trauma based treatment covers education, group and individual sessions and is applicable to a broad range of issues.

I'm not going to say it was easy. There were some days I didn't want to run up the temple stairs, do crunches or face my demons and be brave and vulnerable but you get out what you put in. The first week can be a little scary as you get used to the place but if you commit to the program and trust the process you will find your happy place again. I went specifically for EMDR and felt healed of trauma memories that had plagued me for years.  Happy to be contacted if you want more detail but highly recommend this place.

I’d like to give special thanks to Emmy the nurse and Wine who works in the restaurant. Though I cannot forget Dr Tony, John, Jamie, Conan, Gigi, Pia, Tyler, Bryan, Note, Gabriel, Yamin, Bhum, Mate, Nigh, in fact the whole
Team (I hope I haven’t forgotten anyone!)

The facilities are top-notch, with beautifully appointed treehouses that offer a unique blend of comfort and nature. Each treehouse is equipped with everything you could possibly need, and the attention to detail is evident in every corner. The serene setting provides the perfect backdrop for relaxation and healing.
One of the highlights of my stay was the variety of treatments available. The therapists are highly skilled and attentive, ensuring that each session is tailored to your specific needs. The holistic wellness program, at the Treehouse Treatment Centre has it all. 5 stars!!!

It was a relief to find The Treehouse in Thailand. The location strikes a perfect balance – close enough to city conveniences and attractions for outings, yet wonderfully peaceful by the river with beautifully maintained grounds. The amenities, including the pool, gym, and yoga, are a definite plus, and the rooms are as comfortable as a good city hotel.
However, the staff truly set The Treehouse apart. The nurses are incredibly understanding and patient. What struck me was that many of the support staff have personal experience with addiction, which allows them to connect with clients on a deeper level. I had the pleasure of meeting with the clinical manager, John, who was fantastic. He provided honest and clear updates on progress and consistently sent helpful email updates to my family. Overall, I am very happy with the care and support provided by The Treehouse and wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone considering a stay for themselves or a loved one. It's reassuring to know such a dedicated facility exists here in Thailand.

My experience as a former client was starkly different from what’s promoted. Many of the glowing 5-star reviews appear to be written by staff, interns, or individuals connected to the facility rather than genuine clients. During my stay, I recognized several reviewers as staff members I interacted with, which raises serious concerns about the authenticity of testimonials provided. The website describes a dedicated and compassionate team committed to individualized care, but in reality, I witnessed the owner, Tony, raising his voice and swearing at staff in front of clients.

The site claims that skilled chefs provide nutritious meals for all dietary needs. However, dietary restrictions were often ignored. Meals were not freshly prepared by a chef on site but reheated before meal times, often arriving cold. The limited menu of appetizers and mains quickly became repetitive and boring, and many dishes were far from “nutritious.”
Treehouse Thailand promotes a comprehensive, holistic approach with access to licensed professionals and psychiatrists. In practice, there were no psychiatrists on site. Instead, you receive a brief Zoom call upon arrival with no follow-up or ongoing psychiatric care.

The group sessions often felt like classroom lectures, involving pointless worksheets and waiting around for others to finish, which felt like watching paint dry. Most clients agreed that the group sessions were redundant and failed to provide practical skills that would be useful in the real world. While there were some sessions that were helpful, they were rare. Several groups felt like a waste of time. We’d give feedback to the facility manager, John, which would often be met with excuses or vague promises of improvement, saying “change takes time.”

Eve, one of the psychologists, led art therapy that often repeated the same basic instruction. One week we’d be drawing a road from where we’re at now to where we want to be, the next we’d be told to draw a bridge symbolizing recovery. When we told her it was the exact same instruction as the last activity, just worded differently, she’d refuse to deviate from the plan. All activities were limited to simple materials like crayons or markers on paper, making us feel like we were being held hostage in a kindergarten arts and crafts class.

Our holistic sessions were usually just YouTube audio clips, complete with distracting prompts to “like and subscribe,” making it difficult to meditate. This led to clients walking out mid-way through. Only after external holistic teachers were brought in was there some minor improvement.

The website promotes a range of weekly excursions and adventure therapies like zip lining and river kayaking, but in practice, many of these activities were either unavailable, misleadingly advertised, or poorly organized. Most days, we were confined indoors, so we looked forward to excursions. The client care team often arranged trips where most of the allotted excursion time was spent traveling, or they failed to confirm if destinations were open, resulting in arriving to a closed location and wasted time scrambling for alternatives.

My experience was marked by unmet promises, lack of genuine client focus, and a concerning disregard for both staff and client well-being. I truly believe or at least hope that Tony had good intentions when he started the Treehouse but has lost his way due to the pressures and stress of the job or greed; but getting people to write false reviews, treating staff poorly, and failing to prioritise the wellbeing of vulnerable individuals is not good enough and he needs to re-evaluate the reason why he’s in this.

Overall, did I come out of this a healthier and stronger person? Yes. Would I have gone somewhere else if I had known the downfalls of this facility? Absolutely. Therefore, I strongly encourage anyone considering Treehouse Thailand to seek out authentic, independent client feedback before making a decision.
